name: ci-toolchain-from-rust-toolchain-toml
description: GitHub Actions Rust workflows install the toolchain via dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable with components: rustfmt,clippy and targets: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl set on the action — the action then defers to rust-toolchain.toml for the channel pin, so we never re-specify Rust 1.85 inline. Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 caches target/ + ~/.cargo. Single 'ci' job on ubuntu-latest runs fmt --check → clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings → cargo test → cargo build --release --target musl. Release workflow adds permissions: contents: write and uses softprops/action-gh-release@v2 to upload binary + sha256 on v* tag pushes.

content: CHANGELOG.md follows Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 format with header link + Semver note, contains an empty [Unreleased] section above v0.1.0, and the v0.1.0 entry uses only ### Added (no Changed/Fixed/Deprecated speculation for an initial release). Compare links at the bottom resolve to the canonical GitHub repo at unimatrix099/TeslaGPUFanControl.

name: verify-v0-1-musl-2mb-stripped
description: v0.1 verification (cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, cargo test, host release, musl release): all gates green. Tests: 105 unit + 7 smoke = 112 passed, 1 ignored (softdog watchdog_open_feed_disarm_lifecycle requires root). musl binary at target/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/release/tesla_fan_control is 1990776 bytes (~1.9 MB) stripped static-pie ELF. --version prints 'tesla_fan_control 0.1.0'. --check-config -c config/tesla_fan_control.conf exits 0 silently on canonical operator config. Toolchain auto-installs from rust-toolchain.toml channel 1.85 via dtolnay/non-interactive rustup; musl target is listed in toolchain file so no explicit 'rustup target add' needed.
